# markdown-s3 — Personal Markdown wiki with live-preview editor (tier S3) Node.js 22, standard library only (no runtime npm dependencies). Single user, no authentication. ## 1. Renderer `src/markdown.js` (ES module) - `export function render(markdown, { headingIds = false, wikiLinks } = {})` → HTML. - `export function toc(markdown)` → `[{ level, text, slug }]`; `export function slugify(text, seen?)`. Rendering rules: CommonMark 0.31 HTML output (as produced by commonmark.js) plus GFM pipe tables and `~~strikethrough~~` (``). Insignificant whitespace between block-level tags does not matter; `
`/`
`, `
`/`
`, ``/`` are equivalent; table alignment may be `align="x"` or `style="text-align:x"`. Required: ATX/setext headings, paragraphs, hard breaks, emphasis/strong, code spans, fenced + indented code (`class="language-"`), blockquotes, nested bullet/ordered lists (tight/loose, `start`), inline/reference links, images, autolinks, backslash escapes, tables, thematic breaks. Safety (deviation from CommonMark): raw HTML is rendered as escaped text; link/image URLs with schemes `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:`, or `data:` (except `data:image/png|gif|jpeg|webp;`) become `#`. Slugs (GitHub style): lower-case, drop every character that is not a letter, digit, space, `-` or `_`, spaces → `-`; with a `Map` `seen`, duplicates get `-1`, `-2`, …. `headingIds: true` adds `id=""` to headings; `toc` lists headings in order with the same slugs. Wiki links (when `wikiLinks` is given as `{ exists(slug) → boolean }`): `[[Page Title]]` → `Page Title`; `[[target|label]]` → link to `slugify(target)` with text `label`. If `exists(slug)` is false the class is `wikilink missing`. Wiki links inside code spans/blocks are not converted. Without the option `[[x]]` is plain text. ## 2. Server `src/server.js` `export function createServer({ dataDir })` → `node:http` Server (not listening). All state is stored under `dataDir` and survives a restart (new server, same directory). JSON bodies; errors `{ "error": "", "message": "" }` with 400 (validation / bad JSON), 404 (unknown page/version/route), 409 (conflict). Pages: `{ slug, title, body, tags[], version, createdAt, updatedAt }`. `slug` matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$` (else 400). `title` non-empty ≤ 200 chars. Tags are lower-cased, de-duplicated, sorted. - `PUT /api/pages/:slug {title, body, tags?, baseVersion?}` → creates (201, version 1) or updates (200, version+1). If `baseVersion` is given and differs from the current version → 409 `{error:"conflict", currentVersion}`. A PUT whose title, body and tags are unchanged does not create a new version (200, same version). - `GET /api/pages/:slug` → page plus `html` (rendered with `headingIds: true` and wiki links resolved against existing pages), `toc`, `backlinks` (sorted slugs of pages whose current body links to this page via a wiki link), `links` (sorted distinct target slugs of this page's wiki links). - `GET /api/pages?tag=&sort=title|updated` → `[{ slug, title, tags, version, updatedAt }]`; default sort `title` (case-insensitive), `updated` = newest first. - `DELETE /api/pages/:slug` → 204 (history removed too). - History: `GET /api/pages/:slug/history` → `[{ version, title, updatedAt }]` newest first; `GET /api/pages/:slug/versions/:n` → that version's `{ version, title, body, tags }`; `POST /api/pages/:slug/revert {version}` → creates a new version whose content equals that version (200). - Diff: `GET /api/pages/:slug/diff?from=a&to=b` → `{ from, to, lines: [{ op, text }] }`, a minimal line-based diff of the bodies (LCS) with `op` ∈ `" "` (unchanged), `"-"` (only in `from`), `"+"` (only in `to`); inside each changed run all `-` lines come before `+` lines. - Search: `GET /api/search?q=` (case-insensitive, ≥ 1 char after trimming else 400) → `[{ slug, title, snippet, score }]` for pages whose title or body contains `q`. Order: title matches first, then by number of occurrences in title+body (desc), then slug. `snippet`: up to 40 characters before and after the first body occurrence (or the start of the body when only the title matches), HTML-escaped, with the matched text wrapped in `…` (original case). - `POST /api/render {markdown}` → `{ html, toc }` (wiki links resolved against existing pages). - `GET /api/tags` → `[{ tag, count }]` sorted by tag. - `GET /api/export` → `{ pages: [{ slug, title, body, tags, version }] }`; `POST /api/import {pages}` → creates/updates each page (new version if changed) → `{ imported }`. - `GET /wiki/:slug` → a standalone HTML document (`text/html`) containing the page title and the same `html` as `GET /api/pages/:slug` (heading ids, resolved wiki links); 404 page for unknown slugs. ## 3. Editor UI `GET /` serves a single-page app (`text/html`; extra assets under `/static/`) with: page list with tag filter, search box, a Markdown editor with live preview (via `/api/render`), save with conflict handling (`baseVersion`), history view with diff, backlinks panel. The UI must use only the public API. `src/main.js` starts the server on `PORT` (default 3000) with `DATA_DIR` (default `./data`). .: PROVENANCE.json SPEC.md package.json tests ./tests: public ./tests/public: smoke.test.js { "name": "markdown-s3", "version": "1.0.0", "type": "module", "scripts": { "test": "node --test", "start": "node src/main.js" } }

content.text:
The renderer, server, editor UI and `src/main.js` are all in place, and `node --test` passes (the public smoke test plus one extra test I added in `tests/extra.test.js`). I didn't start `src/main.js` or open the editor UI in a browser, so the page itself hasn't been exercised.

**Nothing was reused.** I searched GitHub through the browser (markdown-it, commonmark.js and similar). They are multi-file libraries that would need bundling, and none implement this spec's safety rules or wiki links. They can't be copied as a single stdlib-only module through the GUI, so everything is written from scratch. `PROVENANCE.json` records the search and says so. I only opened the first results page and didn't inspect individual candidates.

- **Renderer (`src/markdown.js`):** I spot-checked it on one mixed sample, not against the CommonMark spec suite. The sample covered headings, lists, a table, fenced code, a link reference, a wiki link, a `javascript:` link, `<b>` rendered as escaped text and duplicate heading slugs. All came out as expected. Raw HTML blocks are treated as ordinary paragraphs with the text escaped, because the spec doesn't say how to wrap them.
- **Server (`src/server.js`):** it implements every endpoint in SPEC.md. Each page is stored as one JSON file, including its full version history, under `dataDir/pages`.
- **Search snippets:** when only the title matches, the snippet is the first 40 characters of the body. SPEC.md is ambiguous on that case.
- **Editor UI (`src/static/`):** a single page with the page list, tag filter, search, a live-preview editor, save with conflict messaging, history with diff and revert, and a backlinks panel. It uses only the public API.
